We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps correspond to forward reactions: 1) amide formation (carboxylic acid to amide). 2) Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). 3) sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). So retrosynthetic direction: break amide bond to give carboxylic acid and aniline (or aniline derivative). Then break the α,β-unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid? Actually Doebner modification forward: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid (with decarboxylation). So retrosynthesis: the unsaturated acid fragment /C=C/C(=O)N... is product of Doebner: starting from aromatic aldehyde (maybe p-? the aromatic ring attached to sulfonyl) and malonic acid gives the unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid). Then amide formation attaches aniline (c3ccccc3N) to that acid to give amide. So retrosynthesis steps:

Target: aryl-sulfonamide attached to phenyl ring with methyl (p-tolyl) and sulfonyl attached to second phenyl ring bearing α,β-unsaturated amide side chain.

Step 1 (retro): disconnect amide bond between carbonyl and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Gives precursor A: same molecule but with carboxylic acid instead of amide: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1? Wait the amide is C(=O)N attached to aniline. So precursor is the α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1 (i.e., replace N of aniline with OH? Actually the amide carbonyl attached to N of aniline; the acid would be C(=O)O attached to the alkene. So structure: .../C=C/C(=O)O (cinnamic acid). So precursor 1: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1.

Step 2 (retro): disconnect the α,β-unsaturated acid to aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid (or maybe malonic acid decarboxylates to give the acid). The product is cinnamic acid attached to phenyl sulfonyl. So we need to identify the aldehyde precursor: aromatic aldehyde on the second phenyl ring (the one bearing sulfonyl). The aldehyde would be: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2)cc1 (i.e., replace the /C=C/C(=O)O side chain with aldehyde). So precursor 2: same overall but with aldehyde.

Step 3 (retro): disconnect sulfonamide formation: break S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride and aniline (the first phenyl ring with methyl). So precursor 3: sulfonyl chloride attached to second phenyl ring: Cc1ccc(ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2)cc1? Wait sulfonyl chloride is attached to the first phenyl? In target, sulfonamide is NS(=O)(=O) attached to first phenyl (tolyl) nitrogen attached to sulfonyl group which is attached to second phenyl. So sulfonamide formation forward: aniline (first phenyl with NH2) reacts with sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2-Cl) to give sulfonamide. So retro: break N-S bond to give aniline (p-toluidine) and sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2-Cl) where Ar is second phenyl with aldehyde substituent. So precursor 3: p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) and sulfonyl chloride: ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2.

Thus we have three steps: 1) amide formation (acid + aniline). 2) Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid). 3) sulfonamide formation (aniline + sulfonyl chloride). Need to provide route JSON with reactions and template IDs. We need template IDs for each transformation. We have some template IDs from earlier search: For sulfonamide formation, template ID 733 (retro_smarts: [O;D1;H0:2]=[S;...]-[NH...]-[c]>>Cl-[S...]-[c].[NH2...]-[c]) This is a retro template that breaks sulfonamide into sulfonyl chloride and aniline. So we can use template_id 733.

For amide formation (carboxylic acid to amide), need a template that breaks amide into acid and amine. Search maybe with functional_groups_broken: ["carboxylic acid"] and formed: ["amide"] but we got errors due to naming. The functional group for carboxylic acid is "aliphatic carboxylic acid" or "aromatic carboxylic acid". The amide is "amide". So we need to search for templates that form amide (i.e., retro: amide -> acid + amine). Let's search with broken: ["amide"]? Actually forward reaction forms amide, so retro breaks amide. So functional_groups_broken: ["amide"]; functional_groups_formed: ["carboxylic acid","primary amines"] maybe. Let's try search.
